chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, he said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Indeed, Hisham ibn Udhaynah asked me to ask you about a man who stipulated emancipation for his slave if a specific event occurred to his master. The master died, and upon him was the obligation of freeing a slave as expiation (kaffarah). Does the emancipation of the slave, which the master had stipulated for him after his death, suffice for the deceased master in fulfilling the obligation of freeing the slave that was upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.'

key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation (atonement for a sin or obligation)

ai.seo_question: Does a master's stipulated emancipation of a slave upon death count towards his obligatory slave-expiation debt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a master's stipulated emancipation (itq) upon a specific event is a distinct legal obligation from the obligatory slave-expiation (kaffarah) debt, ruling that the former does not satisfy the latter. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific contractual conditions (shurut) do not automatically merge with general religious dues (huquq) unless explicitly intended, ensuring the precision of debt fulfillment in inheritance and manumission cases.
